boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on nearby Foggy Bottom and National Mall corridors, each with one documented reason to stop.

cards.title: Read the names on the Vietnam Veterans Memorial
cards.subtitle: Constitution Avenue NW corridor
cards.notes: Walk the black-granite walls at the west end of the National Mall and use the chronological inscriptions for a quiet, self-guided stop.
cards.short_summary: Maya Lin’s memorial uses two angled granite walls inscribed with names.
cards.evidence_claim: The NPS describes the memorial’s two polished black-granite walls, which carry the names of service members lost or missing in the Vietnam War.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor National Mall memorial; follow posted site guidance.

cards.entity_name: Vietnam Veterans Memorial: Three Servicemen Statue
cards.title: Study the Three Servicemen sculpture
cards.subtitle: Constitution Avenue NW corridor
cards.notes: Find Frederick Hart’s three-figure bronze beside the Vietnam memorial and compare its human-scale detail with the nearby wall.
cards.short_summary: A bronze sculpture added to the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in 1984.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS states that the Three Servicemen statue was added in 1984 and depicts three American servicemen and the things they carried.
cards.source_title: Vietnam Veterans Memorial: Three Servicemen Statue
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial area; follow posted site guidance.

cards.title: Pause at the Vietnam Women’s Memorial
cards.subtitle: Constitution Avenue NW corridor
cards.notes: Visit the bronze group south of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial and take time to notice the three women caring for a wounded soldier.
cards.short_summary: A figurative memorial recognizing women who served during the Vietnam War.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies the Vietnam Women’s Memorial as a sculpture of three uniformed women caring for a wounded male soldier.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor National Mall memorial; follow posted site guidance.

cards.entity_name: Vietnam Veterans Memorial: In Memory Plaque
cards.title: Find the In Memory plaque
cards.subtitle: Constitution Avenue NW corridor
cards.notes: Look in the northeast corner of the Three Servicemen plaza for this later addition honoring Vietnam veterans who died from service-related causes.
cards.short_summary: A 2004 plaque expands the memorial’s act of remembrance.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS says the In Memory plaque, dedicated in 2004, honors Vietnam veterans who later died from causes related to the war.
cards.source_title: Vietnam Veterans Memorial: In Memory Plaque
cards.access_notes: Outdoor memorial area; follow posted site guidance.

cards.title: Cross to Signers Island
cards.subtitle: Constitution Avenue NW corridor
cards.notes: Use the footbridge on the north side of the pond to reach the memorial to the 56 signers of the Declaration of Independence.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped park with a pond, paths, and an island memorial.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS notes that Constitution Gardens has a pond and that Signers Island, with its 56-signers memorial, is reached by footbridge.
cards.access_notes: NPS lists the site as open 24 hours; facilities may close in the evening.

cards.title: Step into the Lincoln Memorial chamber
cards.subtitle: 23rd Street NW corridor
cards.notes: Approach from the Reflecting Pool and view the seated Lincoln statue and interior inscriptions in the memorial’s main chamber.
cards.short_summary: The chamber is the principal public space within the Lincoln Memorial.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS states that the Lincoln Memorial is free and open to the public, including the chamber with the Lincoln statue and symbolic features.
cards.access_notes: The main memorial is free; the lower-level museum and undercroft require timed entry.

cards.title: Follow the 19-statue patrol
cards.subtitle: 23rd Street NW corridor
cards.notes: Walk the memorial’s Field of Service and look for the nineteen stainless-steel figures whose reflections create an image of thirty-eight.
cards.short_summary: A memorial with a field of stainless-steel soldier figures and reflective surfaces.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS describes nineteen stainless-steel statues whose reflections create the visual effect of 38 figures.
cards.access_notes: NPS lists the memorial as open 24 hours a day, every day of the year.

cards.title: Look up inside the DC War Memorial
cards.subtitle: Independence Avenue SW corridor
cards.notes: Step beneath the open circular pavilion south of the Reflecting Pool and look for the names carved around its marble base.
cards.short_summary: A local World War I memorial designed as an open Doric pavilion.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS identifies this as a World War I memorial with an open circular Doric structure and the names of 499 honored Washingtonians.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor National Mall memorial; follow posted site guidance.

cards.title: Walk the World War II Memorial plaza
cards.subtitle: 17th Street NW corridor
cards.notes: Enter the memorial between the Lincoln Memorial and Washington Monument and trace the state and territorial pillars around the central fountain.
cards.short_summary: A National Mall memorial positioned between the Lincoln Memorial and Washington Monument.
cards.evidence_claim: NPS includes the World War II Memorial among the sites preserved by National Mall and Memorial Parks.
cards.source_title: Visit National Mall and Memorial Parks
cards.access_notes: Outdoor National Mall memorial; follow posted site guidance.

cards.title: Visit the Albert Einstein Memorial
cards.subtitle: Constitution Avenue NW corridor
cards.notes: Stop at the National Academy of Sciences grounds to see the Einstein memorial, unveiled for the centennial of the scientist’s birth.
cards.short_summary: A memorial sculpture on the National Academy of Sciences grounds.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Academy of Sciences states that the Albert Einstein Memorial was unveiled in 1979 and stands on the Academy grounds.
cards.access_notes: The memorial is on Academy grounds; the NAS Building itself is closed to the public except for authorized visitors.
